lens: clarity & depth: would a curious 15-year-old follow it and an expert respect it; AlexNet and transformer step by step in sync; each era's belief, dissent, duration
priorRoundsChecked: round-1/teacher.json T01-T18 checked against the current timeline.json and sheets (2026-10-12 20:27). Fixed: T02 (ch08-s03 RGB planes on 'red', count on 'hundred'), T03 (ch10-s09 shuffle held with the 0.58 arc unchanged, clocks on 'clock face'), T04 (L0830 team simile), T06 in substance (new ch06-s03b kernel-trick shot), T07 (L0218 says why, inset enlarged), T08 in part (names voiced, 'lit 2012 · still burning'), T09 in part (match glossed in L1410), T10 (prologue now 150-195 wpm), T11 (8/0/-8 only), T12 (temperature dial removed), T13 (GPT voiced plus Liu/GPT chip), T15 (honest card held ~4 s), T16 (ch12 reordered, Anthropic now one runner), T05 in part (labels RELU, OVERFITTING, SOFTMAX, dropout, TOKENS and gradient descent on screen, none spoken). Partly fixed: T01 (bowl stamped BY HAND and a fog plate added, but the plate is 3.8 s and the learned mosaic never rises), T14 (BLEU gone, but three facts still sit in silence), T18 (horizontal date tags added, candle labels still vertical). Not fixed: art carry-overs ch10-s04 (all-pairs reveal still late), ch05-s04 (no push-in), ch15-s08 (static wide), ch14-s04b (tags still small), ch09-s05 (no Marcus card).
summary: A real step up. The AlexNet dive (ch08-s03..s10, about 2.5 min of mechanism) now runs grid of numbers, three colour planes, 150,528, a worked stencil (-4 clipped to 0, then 3.88) labelled RELU, ninety-six stencils building edges, textures, parts and things, the weir, overfitting on the scale (60M vs 12M) labelled OVERFITTING, crops and mirrors, dropout with the team simile, two GPUs, three step cuts. Every number I checked is right. The transformer dive (ch10-s02..s14) is genuinely expert-grade: Q/K/V cards land on 'question'/'label'/'message'; the dot products (0110·1201=2, 0, 4, 2) and the softmax (0.20/0.07/0.53/0.20) check by hand; 8/0/-8 gives 1.00/0/0 against 0.67/0.24/0.09 after dividing by sqrt(64); the shuffle now shows attention is blind to order; the causal mask and GPT's origin are both there. Classical ML finally has a kernel-trick shot. What still costs clarity is the moment of the transformer itself. On 'every word looks at every other' (ch10-s04, 4.8-6.3 s) the hall shows one beam, and the all-pairs threads arrive only on 'The Transformer'. The backprop plate (ch05-s04), which both deep dives build on, is still framed small, with an unreadable formula card. The new kernel shot packs three ideas into one 12.5 s line, then sits 8.5 s in silence over an unexplained '0 3 1' readout. On depth, the one structural gap left is the symbolic-AI ('Rules') era: it is our 'first suspect' but never gets its own candle, a named dissenter or a duration. Hubert Dreyfus is in the bible (e5-dreyfus, q-dreyfus-pattern) and nowhere in the film. The real terms are now on screen but none is spoken.

issues.problem: Carried over from round 1 and still unfixed: allLight is still at 7.32 and darkBeat at 3.78. Under 'keep the attention' (3.3-4.0) the hall goes nearly black. Under 'every word looks at every other, all at once' (4.8-7.3) the sheet shows a single beam down the hall. The all-pairs threads appear only at about 7.3-8.4, on 'The Transformer', and they fan out from the first five slips only. This is the film's central transformer image, and the viewer hears the idea before seeing it.
issues.fix: Shorten darkBeat to a dip of 0.5 s or less that ends by 3.3. Light every slip on 'every' (4.79), and draw arcs between every pair, far slips included, across 'every other' (5.9-6.3), with all of them bright by 'all at once' (6.9). Bring THE TRANSFORMER banner up on 'Transformer' (8.4) as now.

issues.problem: Backprop is the 'messenger' that both deep dives lean on (L0812, L1010 'tuned by our messenger'), and the push-in has still not been applied. The lantern plate fills about 45% of the frame from 16.8 to 24.0. The blame formula card ('blame(i) = slope(i)·Σ blame(j)·w...') sits at the right edge at about 12 px cap height, unreadable. The +/- tug ticks are present but tiny. After L0509 ends at 30.8, a 4.4 s silent beat shows a Nature quote card before L0521.
issues.fix: Push in to about 70% frame fill from 'messenger' (16.8) through 'blame' (24.0). Double the formula card and set it beside the loom, or drop it and keep the +/- ticks large. Make each knob's tug a visible rotation on 'lantern by lantern' (20.3). Either shorten the 30.8-35.2 silence by 2 s or hold the 1986 quote card at a legible size.

issues.problem: The brief asks for each era's belief, its dissenters and how long it held. Symbolic AI, the 'Rules' suspect (L0215b), is the one major paradigm with no candle, no named dissenter and no duration. The knowledge candle's only dissent is the anonymous 1984 panel. Hubert Dreyfus, the best-known philosophical dissenter, is in the bible (e5-dreyfus; q-dreyfus-pattern, q-dreyfus-gofai) and appears only as a name on a backprop card. An expert will notice he is missing, and a teenager never learns that anyone argued the rules approach was wrong in principle.
issues.fix: Add NEW line L0514b after L0514 in ch05-s07 (about 7 s): 'At its rim stood a philosopher, Hubert Dreyfus: real expertise is intuition, not rules. He saw a pattern: “early, dramatic success followed by sudden unexpected difficulties.”' [e5-dreyfus, q-dreyfus-pattern]. Stand his silhouette at the candle's rim. Optionally, in ch02-s07, also light a 'Rules' candle on 'our first suspect' (L0215b: 'intelligence is symbols and rules', lit 1956) so that Lighthill (ch04-s06) and the chess slip (ch06-s07) have a flame to strike.

issues.problem: The new classical-recipe shot fixes the gap in substance, but L0607b crams the hand-cut features, the learner, the kernel lift and the moral into 12.5 s (174 wpm). The lift itself gets about 1.5 s (6.5-8.0). Nothing says what the '2 4 0' readout is. Then 8.5 s of silence (12.5-21.0) shows a second readout, '0 3 1', that is never explained. A 15-year-old sees numbers in a box and a ziggurat.
issues.fix: Use the silent tail and split L0607b into two lines. (a) 'An expert chose what to measure, by hand; the machine only drew the line.' Label the readout 'features, chosen by hand', and land the second readout here as a second example. (b) 'When no straight line would do, the kernel trick lifted one crowd up a hill, and one flat cut parted them. The learning was clean; the seeing was hand-made.' Hold the lifted cone and glass plane for at least 3 s on 'lifted... flat cut'.

issues.problem: Round-1 T01 is only partly fixed. The bowl with a BY HAND stencil strip now lands on 'clean bowl ... cut by hand' (20.3-22.1), which is good. But the fog plate holds only 23.9-27.7, and on 'the net cut its own' (25.8-26.3) only a few tiny drifting specks rise. 'Many layers deep: deep learning' (26.9-29.1) plays over the shelf again, so the film's thesis line ends without its picture.
issues.fix: Hold the fog plate to 29.2. On 'cut its own' (25.8), raise the learned stencil mosaic from ch08-s06 out of the fog, at least a quarter of the frame. On 'many layers deep' (26.9), stack it into the ch08-s05 tower silhouette. Return to the shelf only for L0832b.

issues.problem: The three export-control positions ('DECISIVE' Amodei/Khan, 'HELPS HUAWEI' Huang, 'SELF-DEFEATING' China MFA) are still small tags, about 14 px caps at 1080p. They pop in within about 1.5 s of each other in the 1.6 s gap between L1410 and L1410b, and none is voiced. The shot then ends with 4.5 s of silence (10.8-15.3).

If a line can be afforded: 'Some called the chip rules decisive; Nvidia's chief said they helped Huawei; Beijing called them self-defeating.'

issues.problem: BLEU is gone, but three facts still appear in the 3.4 s silence between L1025 and L1027: '12 hours', 'one machine, 8 GPUs' and '≈ 1/7 the compute'. The '1/7 the compute' card arrives at 11.9 and is gone by 13.5.
issues.fix: Keep the sundial plus '12 hours' and 'one machine, 8 GPUs' as a single card. Drop '1/7 the compute', or hold it 2 s or longer by trimming the matrix beat.

issues.problem: The card '55 · 27 · 13 · 13 · 13 → 4096 · 4096 · 1000' (from 14.1 to the end) gives spatial sizes that no viewer can decode and that the narration never mentions. It competes with the '≈60 million numbers / 650,000 neurons' card the line actually supports.

issues.problem: This is the only line over 200 wpm (224), and it fails QA pacing. 'A bad back kept Hinton from flying. Yann LeCun stood at the rear of a packed room' runs into the Florence reveal, the dramatic peak of the AlexNet chapter.
issues.fix: Re-narrate it solo at speed about 0.88 with a breath after 'flying'. Let ch08-s11 grow by about 1 s, then re-fit the m11 cue.

issues.problem: The trade terms now appear as synced labels (RELU, OVERFITTING, SOFTMAX, dropout p = 0.5, gradient descent, TOKENS), which is a clear improvement. But none is ever spoken. TOKENS ('models read word-pieces, not whole words') shows while the narration says 'predict the next word', so the expert's quibble remains.
issues.fix: Voice two terms at most, as half-lines: L1013 '...About half runs to river: softmax, to the trade.' and L1103 '...predict the next word, or rather, the next word-piece.' Keep the others as labels.

issues.problem: The film's recap ('Not rules alone. Not knowledge... data, fire, a messenger, and people choosing') plays over a static wide of the case board from 4.8 to 15.3. Every card is about 40 px, so the viewer cannot match the spoken accomplices to the pictures, and the payoff of 35 minutes of setup blurs.
issues.fix: Make short pushes to each card on its word: rules 6.34, knowledge 7.74, Learning 9.93, data 11.77, fire 12.49, messenger 13.36, people 14.52. Pull back on 'Never one person' (16.0) for the board-becomes-network reveal.

issues.problem: The doubters are now named and the candle is dated, which is good. But the Marcus 2018 'Critical Appraisal' card routed in round 1 is absent, so the rim offers only bias and adversarial examples, not the 'deep learning will hit a wall' critique that ch11-s08 later assumes the viewer knows.
issues.fix: In the silent tail (21.0-24.9), pin a horizontal name card: 'Gary Marcus, 2018: “Deep Learning: A Critical Appraisal”' [e9-marcus]. Hold it at least 2 s at a legible size.

issues.problem: 'Each word arrives as a learned list of numbers' (0.6-3.0): the six-number column appears at about 4.6, on 'three cards', and has faded by 5.5. So the link between the word's numbers and its three cards is never drawn. The knobs that make the cards appear only at 12.6.
issues.fix: Bring the number column in on 'numbers' (3.0) and keep it visible. On 'question' (5.5), 'label' (7.9) and 'message' (10.0), draw a thin thread from the column through a small knob bank to each card, so each card visibly comes from the same numbers turned by different knobs.

best_moments: ch10-s06: an attention computation a teenager can check by hand. 0110·1201 = 2, then 0, 4, 2, halved to 1, 0, 2, 1; the SOFTMAX jug pours 0.20/0.07/0.53/0.20 (correct), and bank's meaning tints toward water. Each number lands on its spoken word.

ch10-s07: why divide by the square root of d_k, now clean. Only 8/0/-8 is shown; it tips 1.00/0/0 ('learning freezes'), against 1/0/-1 pouring 0.67/0.24/0.09 ('learning flows'), with the real formula underneath and the callback that our toy's halving was the square root of 4.

ch10-s09 (fixed): the shuffle holds the 0.58 bank→river arc unchanged while the words scramble, which proves attention is blind to order. Then clock faces land on 'clock face' and the fast/slower/slowest waves on 'fast, some slow'.

ch08-s04: the pierced-tin stencil as a true edge kernel. -4 is clipped to 0 under a RELU label, the next position gives max(0, ...) = 3.88, and sliding it everywhere lights the outline of the 4 on 'convolution'.
ch08-s03 (fixed): Rosenblatt's 20×20 = 400 Mark I grid dissolves into a 2012 photo; the RGB planes fan out on 'red, green, blue', and '224 × 224 × 3 = 150,528' lands on 'hundred and fifty thousand'.

ch08-s08: overfitting as a balance scale. 60,000,000 weights against 1.2 million labels × ≈10 bits ≈ 12 million, the OVERFITTING label landing on 'memorise', then crops and mirrors (×2048) piling onto the light pan.
ch10-s14: the decoder-only cut with 'Liu et al., Google, Jan 2018 · OpenAI GPT, June 2018', then a German causal-mask grid where 'auf' can look only back. The curtain is literal.

ch02-s08 (fixed): the frog's-eye inset, now a third of the frame, lights a moving bug pattern while the line says the eye itself was already sorting the world. The logic-machine candle then gutters, with its 16 years ticked off.

ch04-s01 and the candle shelf: XOR with scissors (one cut fails, two cuts and a hidden layer succeed), and a shelf that gives nearly every era a belief, a rim dissenter and a duration (16, ~7, 17, ~7, 13, 10-15, 20, 39, ~2 years).
